subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Striking with Short and Long Implements
title: Performance task build: forehand and backhand contact
essentialQuestion: How does the implement change the way I strike?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Backhand: turn the shoulder further and lead with the knuckles.
Contact in front of the body for both.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Running around the backhand to avoid it. Fix: set a rule that alternate shots must be backhand.
keyPoints: Backhand: turn the shoulder further and lead with the knuckles.
Contact in front of the body for both.
privacySafeScenario: Rally cooperatively with two different implements and explain how grip, contact point, and follow-through changed between them.
studentTask: The learner practises forehand and backhand contact at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with forehand and backhand contact and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about forehand and backhand contact at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for forehand and backhand contact.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Striking may use a hand, a short paddle, or a long implement; a balloon, beach ball, or ball on a tee; and a shorter or seated swing. A learner may also call the contact point and follow-through for a partner instead of striking.
extensionChallenge: Apply forehand and backhand contact under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises forehand and backhand contact. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
